changes: A product phase spec is now its ideal state: three levels (Done, Good, Surprising), criteria and anti-criteria with ids (`C1`, `A1`), and the probe that would prove each one false. A person confirms Done and Good before building starts, and the spec stays after the phase is done.

The Product phase playbook works from the spec's failing criteria, runs each probe before and after a change, lists the criteria a PR moves with evidence (`P1-C3`), and adds a feature to a done phase as new unchecked criteria that reopen it. When you reject work whose criteria passed, it adds the missing criterion first.

`check-product.py` checks the new spec: the three levels and a `**Confirmed.**` line, a probe on every criterion and anti-criterion, unique ids, `Evidence:` on every checked box, a confirmation before a phase is Planned, Building, In progress or Gated, and no unchecked box in a Done phase.
Breaking for product repos: specs with an `## Acceptance` checklist fail `check-product.py` until upgraded. scaffold-product has an upgrade mode that converts them in one PR.
entries.try: /scaffold-product upgrade this repo's phase specs to the ideal-state format

changes: New `root-cause` skill finds a bug's root cause from facts instead of from reading the code, for agent-written or unfamiliar code. `rootcause.py` keeps the case (facts against a control, hypotheses, and the matrix between them), says the one next step, refuses a new hypothesis before the tactics are tried or while several survive, and refuses a root cause until exactly one hypothesis explains every fact and an adversarial review on another model has passed it.

`rootcause.py report` writes the evidence, what was ruled out and by which fact, and the layers the agent couldn't reach as infrastructure work. `rootcause.py recheck` reruns each fact's check and fails while a bug-only signal still holds, so a solved case can gate a deploy.
The Bug fix and Perf issue playbooks send the agent to `root-cause` when the code is unfamiliar or two theories have failed.

changes: The weekly quality brief no longer stops in a Claude Code cloud session: it checks GitHub access with a real `gh api` call, not `gh auth status`, which fails there even when access works. It also says what to do when every artifact download is refused.

`qualitydirector` has the weekly quality brief as numbered steps (`references/weekly-brief.md`): fetch the week's CI test records, book them, summarize, write the brief from the books' template with at most three proposals, check, and open one pull request for sign-off.

`quality.py ingest` books the test-run artifacts CI uploads into the quality books (`runs.csv`, the new `failures.csv`, and `tests-weekly.csv`), rejecting any malformed file by name and booking the rest, and it changes nothing the second time you run it.

`quality.py summary --json` gives one weekly object (suite time against the prior four weeks, slowest tests, failures on push, flaky tests, tests added and removed, the 300-second threshold), so a brief copies numbers instead of computing them.
`quality.py record --sha SHA` records the commit you name, so a pull_request run books the PR head instead of GitHub's temporary merge commit.

`quality.py fetch` downloads the test-results artifacts of the repos in the new `books/watched.csv` through `gh`, with GitHub's own account of each run, and `ingest` believes that account for who a run is (repo, commit, event, workflow, start, link) and a recorder file only for what it measured, so a forged or impersonating artifact cannot put a wrong row into the append-only books. Two conflicting files for one run book neither.

`quality.py ingest` and `check` refuse test ids and other cells that a spreadsheet would run or a terminal would obey, cells over 1000 characters, files over 8 MB or 20000 tests, and starts outside 2020 to 2099; one bad file no longer blocks the others.

A test with both an `error` and a `fail` line in one run is booked as `error`. Books layout changes again: a books folder needs `books/watched.csv` (`repo,github,workflow`), and `failed_on_main` is the failures in pushes to the default branch.
The recorder now leaves SIGINT ignored when it starts that way, as plain unittest does, and a test that runs another suite inside itself no longer turns the outer test red.
Books layout changes: `tests-weekly.csv` has `total_ms` where it had `p50_ms`, and a books folder without `failures.csv` fails `check`.

changes: New `qualitydirector` skill records a unittest run as per-test time and outcome (`quality.py record`), so you can see what a repo's suite costs and which tests are slow or failing. A run that is cut short, an empty suite or a module that fails to import counts as a failure, never a green run.
`quality.py check` validates the quality books (`runs.csv` and `tests-weekly.csv`) and, with `--base REF`, fails if a past run row was edited or removed.
